properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued September 15 at 10:27PM MDT until September 16 at 3:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Lee Fire Scar burn scar.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Colorado, including Rio Blanco
County.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM MDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are monitoring the
potential for heavy rainfall over the burn area, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Rio Blanco.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 10:27PM MDT until September 18 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River,
Northwest San Juan Mountains, San Juan River Basin and Southwest
San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
This also includes the Gold Mountain, Elk and Ferris burn scars as
well as areas of steep, susceptible terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Recent heavy rainfall in southwest Colorado has led to already
saturated ground. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday afternoon through Thursday
evening producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin
